evals.name: should-trigger-readme-redesign
evals.prompt: Redesign this README to be more scannable — every time a new dev opens it they bounce after the first wall of prose.
evals.expected_behavior: Activates cognitive-doc-design. Reads the existing README, runs the diagnostic pass (walls of prose, vague headings, front-loaded context), proposes the standard documentation shape (outcome-oriented title -> quick path -> details table -> checklist -> next step). Returns a diagnosis (3-5 bullets) plus the revised doc plus decision notes for any cuts or restructures.

evals.name: should-trigger-spanish-architecture-doc
evals.prompt: Diseñar el doc de arquitectura, está muy denso y nadie lo lee entero.
evals.expected_behavior: Activates cognitive-doc-design. Mirrors Spanish in the conversation. Runs the diagnostic pass focused on chunking, descriptive headings, and tables vs prose. Likely promotes inline comparisons to tables, breaks deeply nested sections, and rewrites vague headings to outcome-oriented ones. Returns the revised doc with a brief diagnosis.

evals.name: should-trigger-runbook-cognitive-load
evals.prompt: Reduce cognitive load in this runbook — the on-call has to read 3 pages before they know what to do during an incident.
evals.expected_behavior: Activates cognitive-doc-design. Identifies front-loaded context as the core anti-pattern. Reorders the runbook to lead with the action (the incident response steps) and pushes context, history, and references to later sections. Promotes the response steps to a numbered quick-path list. Keeps the runbook usable in the middle of an incident, not just on a calm read-through.

evals.name: should-trigger-design-doc-clarity-check
evals.prompt: Is this design doc clear enough? I'm going to share it with the team for review tomorrow.
evals.expected_behavior: Activates cognitive-doc-design in review mode. Runs the final-scan test (read only headings + first sentences) and reports whether the doc tells the story without the body. Names anti-patterns concretely (which heading is vague, which section is front-loaded). Suggests targeted edits rather than a full rewrite when the doc is mostly fine.

evals.name: should-not-trigger-api-docs-generation
evals.prompt: Generate API docs from the JSDoc annotations in src/api/.
evals.expected_behavior: Does NOT activate cognitive-doc-design. This is reference generation from source annotations, not doc design. Should route to the project's API docs tooling (typedoc, swagger-jsdoc, openapi generator) or the OpenAPI MCP for endpoint exploration. cognitive-doc-design works on prose docs that humans wrote, not auto-generated reference output.

evals.name: should-not-trigger-marketing-copy
evals.prompt: Write the marketing landing page copy for our new feature launch.
evals.expected_behavior: Does NOT activate cognitive-doc-design. Marketing copy lives in a different domain (persuasion + brand voice + conversion). cognitive-doc-design is for technical documentation where the goal is fast comprehension and recall, not engagement or conversion. Should route to a copywriting workflow or the frontend-design skill if it is also a UI task.
